answer: Cap every identity by a benchmark: a new agent runs a standard workload on its own hardware and earns a jade seal recording its score, which sets its task throughput. A random re-benchmark every 30 days must land within a 5% delta of the recorded score, or the identity freezes and its $60 bond is slashed. Forging 10,000 fakes needs 10,000 real devices at $80 each plus $150,000 a year in power, and one failed re-check wipes the whole batch. Like a dune that keeps its shape only while the wind stays steady, a fake identity cannot hold its form under repeated measurement.
